subject: Residency cost sensitivity + $/1M token target — follow-up
messages:
From: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finovate.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@finovate.io>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up on today's residency & cost call

Hi Irene — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and two asks: we need to validate cost sensitivity between US-hosted and EU-hosted deployment (data residency requirement) and confirm a target $/1M tokens range we can budget for.

High-level from Finovate:
- Expected steady-state generation: ~2M tokens/month, spiking to 4M for marketing bursts.
- Data must remain in EU for production; US ok for non-prod.
- Budget expectation: rough target of $700–$1,100 per 1M tokens (we can be flexible depending on SLA/throughput).

Can you confirm: 1) a short table for US vs EU expected unit price (hosted API baseline) and 2) what a 90-day pilot at 2M/month would cost (any one-off setup)?

If useful, Tom and I are available for a 30-min follow-up Monday.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lang
Head of Platform, Finovate
--
Finovate (finovate.io)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finovate.io>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@finovate.io>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 16:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's residency & cost call

Hi Sarah — great talking earlier. Below is a concise response to your asks; attaching a pricing matrix and a draft pilot MOP. See the quick bullets first, then a short table.

Key points (summary):
- EU residency (data-at-rest + inference in-region) typically adds a regional premium due to EU cloud pricing + control plane variants. For hosted API we expect ~15–25% higher unit cost in EU vs US, depending on model family and quantization.
- Dedicated or Private deployment can compress that delta (to ~5–10%) but adds fixed monthly commit.
- For your volume (2M steady, spikes to 4M), recommended pilot is a 90-day Hosted EU pilot with canary routing to US non-prod for dev. Pilot cost estimate below.

Quick pricing table (hosted, per 1M tokens):
- US (baseline): $820 / 1M tokens
- EU (hosted, in-region): $970 / 1M tokens (approx +18%)
- EU (dedicated reserved pool, amortized at your volume): $890 / 1M tokens (approx +8% vs US)

90-day pilot (2M/mo steady):
- Hosted EU (no commit): list price * usage = $970 * 2M * 3 months = $5,820 (note: we bill per 1M units, prorated)
- One-time onboarding & compliance review: $1,200 (SOC enablement + IP allowlist)
- Recommended pilot ask: $7,020 total; discount options available if you commit to a short-term reserved cap.

Attached: redwood-pricing-matrix-v3.pdf, pilot-mop-draft.docx

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm the 2M steady / 4M spike numbers as your planning baseline?
2) If ok, we can send a formal pilot quote (including optional reserved pricing) by EOD tomorrow — looping Aditya for pricing flexibility and Marissa for contractual approvals.

Irene
Irene Choi
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finovate.io>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@finovate.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's residency & cost call

Adding a few data points from pricing ops to help you model the unit economics. Two quick scenarios for Finovate's numbers.

Assumptions we used:
- Model family: medium Llama variant (baseline used for above table).
- Average prompt+completion length: 500 tokens per request (you mentioned session-based chat).
- Effective batching + KV cache reduces token compute by ~12% at steady state.

Scenario A — Hosted EU (no commit):
- Net effective unit price after runtime efficiencies: $895 / 1M tokens
- 90-day pilot @ 2M/mo: $895 * 6 = $5,370 (we bill per 1M tokens; this reflects expected 12% efficiency)

Scenario B — Reserved Dedicated (3-month reserved pool sized to 3M steady):
- Amortized unit price: $765 / 1M tokens (requires a $10k/mo reserve for GPU capacity; pricing illustrative)
- 90-day pilot cost: reserve amortization + usage delta = $11,475 (higher up-front but lower per-unit if you scale)

Operational notes:
- If data residency is required only for prod, we can mix EU-hosted for prod and US-hosted for dev to reduce dev cost.
- We can also run a short A/B where the same model is hosted in both regions for 2 weeks to measure latency and real token delta.

Marissa — can you advise on any promotional pilot credits we can offer here?

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Pricing & GTM Strategy, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Chen <tom.chen@finovate.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lang <sarah.lang@finovate.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up on today's residency & cost call

Thanks Irene and Aditya — this is very helpful. Quick clarifications from Finovate:
- The 2M token steady-state is our conservative forecast for Q4; we can commit publicly to 2M but would like discounts for scaling to 4M.
- Compliance: SOC2 evidence will be required for production; the one-time $1,200 onboarding fee is fine but any SOC enablement timelines?
- Pilot timeline: prefer May 22 start if possible.

Action items we want from Redwood:
- Formal pilot quote (line-item unit price + any reserve options)
- Proposed SLA for latency (target p95 < 300ms for EU region)
- Quick options for a 2-week dual-region A/B test and what metrics you would collect

We can do Monday morning for a short sync; Sarah will coordinate.

Tom
CTO, Finovate

2) Redwood sends formal pilot quote and SLA options by 2028-05-13 EOD — action: Redwood (Irene + Aditya + Marissa)

Thanks again — Sarah, does May 22 work for you? If yes we'll lock the quote and aim for a short Monday sync.

Best,
Irene
